kind: Actual local-browser prototype comparison; readback-inclusive serial completed-frame latency on software WebGL; not real-device FPS or a pure engine speed comparison.

method.fixture: Same Blender-exported GLB and exact clip times, full source geometry, same camera/drawing buffer/DPR, independent WebGL contexts, no rAF/adaptive quality/LOD. Actual GL draw instrumentation and framebuffer reads; no mocked scene or animation.
method.measurement: cpuUpdateMs measures animation/pose update; submitMs measures GL submission; completedFrameMs includes update + submit + gl.finish + synchronous 1x1 RGBA8 readPixels. A separate identical readback drains the previous frame before the timer. First frame and load are separate from warmed samples.
method.completionFence: A native 1px RGBA8 readPixels is required. Diagnostic testing found gl.finish alone returned in 0.5–3.4ms while a following readPixels still waited 27–81ms on this Chromium/SwiftShader adapter.
limitations: DQS custom versus LBS Three can produce different skin surfaces with matching bone matrices.
Custom uses one combined material-ID draw per actor; Three renders ten glTF material primitives.
PBR BRDF/tone mapping and material coverage differ despite matched inputs; screenshots require human judgment.
Completed-frame latency includes a 4-byte synchronous readback and driver/browser synchronization; it is not a GPU timer.
SwiftShader serial latency does not predict hardware throughput or device FPS.

coldLoads.kind: Fresh browser context; module imports complete; first uncached asset fetch/parse/texture readiness. Custom shader creation may occur in load; Three may compile lazily on first frame.
